lesson.title: Modal Gym
lesson.subtitle: kan, moet, mag, wil, zal — five modals, one shape

hook.title: Five Modals, One Shape
hook.content: Kan, moet, mag, wil, zal: five different meanings, one sentence shape. Modal second, infinitive last. The vocabulary changes; the bracket does not.

pattern.title: Meaning changes, position stays
pattern.content: Ik kan gaan, jij moet blijven, wij willen komen, zij mag gaan. The modal agrees with the subject; the infinitive never does.
pattern.trap_note: Zal is not English 'shall' in every context; it often marks future or intention. Learn the shape first, then the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Modal Gym):
exercises.target_answer: kunnen, moeten, mogen, willen, gaan, blijven
exercises.meaning: to be able to, to have to, must, to be allowed to, to want, to go, to stay
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Modal Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Ik kan gaan.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Modal Gym”.

cues: The pattern: Meaning changes, position stays
exercises.explanation: “Jij moet blijven.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Meaning changes, position stays.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Zal is not English 'shall' in every context; it often marks future or intention. Learn the shape first, then the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Wij willen komen.” is word-for-word “We want to come.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Meaning changes, position stays.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: “Zij mag gaan.” reuses only material taught in “Modal Gym” — Meaning changes, position stays.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Zij mag gaan.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Meaning changes, position stays.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I do not want to work.”
twist.explanation: Niet precedes the final infinitive; the modal remains second.

summary.outcome: Swap five modals through the same bracket without changing the second verb.
summary.takeaway: A modal is a slot, not a new sentence pattern.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Separable Verbs.

kunnen.etymology_derivation: English can and Dutch kunnen are the same modal root.

moeten.etymology_derivation: English must and Dutch moeten are the same modal root.

mogen.etymology_derivation: English may and Dutch mogen are the same modal root.

willen.etymology_derivation: English will (as desire) and Dutch willen are the same verb.

gaan.etymology_derivation: The same verb as English go, with the old g still pronounced.

blijven.etymology_derivation: English stay is a different verb; Dutch blijven is the direct Germanic twin of German bleiben.
